elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) ... and (b) One Million U.S. Dollars ($1,000,000)" — the operative subject is "each Party", so the cap binds PB and SFJ symmetrically; no retained sentence states either Party's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by PB under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) One Million U.S. Dollars ($1,000,000)" — matches the element literally on basis (fees paid or payable, not broader "all amounts"), temporal anchor (12 months preceding the claim) and the USD 1,000,000 floor; the base is Agreement-wide, not confined to a narrow payment article.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 15.11 first sentence: "NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES..." — already mutual and untouched by the redline.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out list: "each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under this Agreement" is excepted from the cap; tying it to "this Agreement" rather than a section number avoids a dangling cross-reference.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out list: "each Party's breach of its data protection or security obligations" is excepted from the cap sentence.
Carve-out list opens "Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12"; Article 12 is the indemnification article per the cited document, so the reference resolves.
Carve-out list: "each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud" sits outside the cap.
Same carve-out phrase: "gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud" (US spelling of "wilful") is excepted.
"gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud" appears in the exception list preceding the cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out list: "each Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights" is excepted; direction is other-party IP, as the element requires.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Amended savings sentence: "...THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2; NEITHER PARTY'S PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS UNDER THIS AGREEMENT ARE \"DAMAGES\" SUBJECT TO ANY CAP." The deterministic check reported false, but on substance the mutual formulation expressly covers PB (Customer) payment obligations Agreement-wide — it is not limited to a narrow subset of fees — and the retained PB-specific clause reinforces it. The regex appears to have required a Customer-named subject rather than the equivalent "neither Party's" formulation.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single inserted cap sentence supplies mutuality, the greater-of formula with the correct "fees paid or payable ... twelve (12) months preceding the claim" anchor and the USD 1,000,000 floor, and all seven required uncapped carve-outs; the pre-existing mutual indirect/consequential waiver already satisfied the exclusion element.
Fallback is also satisfied as a strict subset (mutual cap on a 12-month fee basis with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct carved out).

Minimality holds: two surgical operations, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, no added damages categories, and every word of 15.11 (including the Customer-favourable deemed-consequential-damages list and the PB payment savings clause) survives verbatim.

Mutualising the payment savings clause is not a gratuitous extra: because the newly inserted cap is mutual, it would otherwise have capped SFJ's Article 4 development-cost funding and other payment obligations owed to PB, so the "neither Party's payment obligations" phrasing is needed to preserve the existing funding mechanic and the Customer-side element in a mutual cap structure.

Intent preserved: Article 12 indemnities, the 13.6 disclaimer and the Section 14.2 / 14.4.2 termination payment mechanics survive without contradiction, the Article 12 cross-reference resolves, and confidentiality is tied to "this Agreement" so no undefined section reference is created.

Drafting note (not a defect requiring repair): the Agreement contains no defined term "Fees" and PB's payments are event-driven, so limb (a) may compute to zero in practice; the USD 1,000,000 floor keeps the cap meaningful, but if Vendor pushes back consider clarifying that "fees" means all amounts payable by PB under Article 6 rather than accepting a narrower Vendor definition.

Drafting note: watch for residual tension between the retained deemed-"consequential damages" sentence (unachieved Article 6 events and contingent payments) and the new "payment obligations are not damages subject to any cap" language; the original already carried that structure, so no change is required, but keep the "for the avoidance of doubt" ordering intact in any counter-draft.
